findings: Re-pin window on the first Probe of a round is contradictory: turn structure step 4 (section 4) says any 'failed Probe' opens a re-pin window with no exception, but the Re-pin action rules say the Locksmith 'may not re-pin ... after the opening Probe.' Unclear whether the first Probe of every round is categorically barred from triggering a re-pin, or whether that line just restates that the Locksmith can't yet afford the 2-point cost.

Tiebreak step 3, 'Highest single opening score (the biggest rail number anyone banked)', does not say whether 'anyone' is scoped to the tied players or to any player in the game. If scoped to all players, it can fail to separate two tied players when a third, non-tied player holds the highest banked opening.

Tiebreak steps 2 ('most locks opened as a Cracker across the whole game') and 3 ('highest single opening score') require per-player history across all rounds, but no printed component (score board, round board, deduction card) records either history — the score board only shows current point totals, not counts of opens or past opening values.
